review_notes: Source-first scope: retain Table 3 full-period attenuation trends for the two outcomes the introduction identifies as central: anomaly hedge-portfolio returns (Panel A) and monthly Fama–MacBeth characteristic premiums (Panel B). Include 12 anomaly-specific series plus the equally weighted hedge composite for NYAM; use the Table 2 monthly cross-sectional regression as required construction for Panel B.

Population choice: NYAM is the paper’s stated base sample (1976–2011). Nasdaq results are reported in parallel but use a shorter sample beginning in 1983; under the principal-base-sample boundary, they are not included as an additional family. Table 4–6 discovery/period/decimalization and arbitrage-proxy analyses are follow-up explanations and are excluded.

Table 3 hedge outcomes are raw returns. Do not import the factor risk adjustment used for the FM characteristic-premium outcome into the hedge-return trends. The supplied source states an equally weighted high-decile-long/low-decile-short formation rule, but the later R1 interpretation describes the reverse direction while attaching it to the same negative Table 2 return; preserve this genuine conflict.

The source gives log turnover in its Section 2 definition and gives the underlying monthly volume/shares ratio in Table 2/3 notes; the latter does not state an incompatible unlogged transformation. BM and TURN log bases are unreported; R212 aggregation and ISSUE denominator/scaling are also unreported.

Recursive fitted inputs retained: first-pass full-sample factor regressions generate the risk-adjusted return used in monthly Fama–MacBeth cross-sections; daily FF3 residual fits generate IVOL. The IVOL fit is linked to its hedge return and the EW composite. No method is inferred from linear appearance or from a family name.
